source_text: Orabat autem Dominus et rogabat non pro se — quid enim pro se innocens precaretur? — sed pro delictis nostris, sicut et ipse declarat cum dicit ad Petrum: ecce satanas postulabat ut uos uexaret quomodo triticum. ego autem rogaui pro te, ne deficiat fides tua. et postmodum pro omnibus patrem deprecatur dicens:: non pro his autem rogo solis sed et pro illis qui credituri sunt per uerbum ipsorum in me, ut omnes unum sint, sicut et tu pater in me et ego in te, ut et ipsi in nobis sint. magna Dei propter salutem nostram benignitas pariter et pietas, ut non contentus quod nos sanguine suo redimeret adhuc pro nobis amplius et rogaret. rogantis autem desiderium uidete quod fuerit, ut quomodo unum sunt pater et filius, sic et nos in ipsa unitate maneamus: ut hinc quoque possit intellegi quantum delinquat qui unitatem scindit et pacem, cum pro hoc et rogauerit Dominus uolens scilicet plebem suam uiuere, cum sciret ad regnum Dei discordiam non uenire.
orientation: Cyprian is explaining that the Lord prayed not for himself but for our sins and for the unity of all believers.
pass_a_gloss: He was praying [then] the Lord and he was asking not for himself — what [indeed] for himself [as] innocent would he pray? — but for our sins, just as [also] he himself declares when he says to Peter: behold Satan was asking that he might vex you [all] like wheat. I [however] have asked for you, that [not] fail your faith. And afterwards for all [people] the Father he beseeches saying: not for these [however] I ask only but [also] for those who are going to believe through the word of them in me, that all one may be, just as [also] you Father in me and I in you, that [also] they in us may be. Great [is] God's for our salvation kindness [equally] and piety, that not content that he [with] his blood us redeemed [still] for us more [also] he asked. Of the one asking [however] the desire see what it was, that just as one are the Father and the Son, so [also] we in that same unity may remain: that from this [also] can be understood how much he sins who unity splits and peace, since for this [also] asked the Lord wishing [namely] his people to live, since he knew [that] to the kingdom of God discord [does] not come.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the comparison; 'quomodo' here means 'like' or 'as'
Literal rendering of the purpose clause
rejected: so that everyone might be united

choices.why: Keeps the paired nouns distinct and the force of 'pariter' as 'likewise'

choices.english: may remain in that same unity
choices.why: Preserves the demonstrative force of 'ipsa' and the subjunctive of purpose

choices.term: ad regnum Dei discordiam non uenire
choices.english: discord does not come to the kingdom of God
choices.why: Literal word order and meaning; 'uenire ad' means 'come to'
rejected: discord has no place in God's kingdom

pass_b_english: But the Lord was praying and asking not for himself—what would an innocent man ask for himself?—but for our sins, as he himself makes clear when he says to Peter: “Behold, Satan demanded to have you, to vex you like wheat. But I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail” (Luke 22:31-32). And afterward he prays to the Father for all, saying: “I am not praying for these alone, but also for those who are going to believe in me through their word, that all may be one, just as you, Father, are in me and I in you, that they also may be in us” (John 17:20-21). Great is God’s kindness and likewise his love for our salvation, that he was not content to redeem us with his blood, but still prayed for us as well. See what the desire of the one praying was: that just as the Father and the Son are one, so we also may remain in that same unity. From this it can be understood how greatly the one sins who splits unity and peace, since the Lord prayed for this very thing, wanting his people to live, knowing that discord does not come to the kingdom of God.

last_rejected.quote: Satan demanded to have you, to vex you like wheat
last_rejected.source_quote: ecce satanas postulabat ut uos uexaret quomodo triticum
last_rejected.why: Latin says Satan asked to vex 'you' plural (vos), not 'you' singular Peter alone; Jesus says he prayed for Peter (te) specifically.
last_rejected.fix: Behold, Satan demanded to have you all, to sift you like wheat. But I have prayed for you [Peter], that your faith may not fail
last_rejected.ruling: 'you' is ambiguous in English, covers both singular and plural; reader is not misled.

last_rejected.quote: that he was not content to redeem us with his blood, but still prayed for us as well
last_rejected.source_quote: ut non contentus quod nos sanguine suo redimeret adhuc pro nobis amplius et rogaret
last_rejected.why: Latin 'adhuc pro nobis amplius et rogaret' = 'still he prayed even more for us.' English 'but still prayed for us as well' loses 'amplius' = 'more'/'further'/'even more.' The emphasis on additional, greater prayer is weakened. But 'as well' captures some of this. Is this major? The 'amplius' = 'more' is significant—Christ not only redeemed but prayed even more. English 'still prayed for us as well' is weaker but not wrong. Hmm, let me check if 'amplius' could mean 'furthermore' here. Yes, 'amplius' = 'further'/'moreover'/'even more.' The English loses the comparative force. But is it major? The meaning is substantially the same—he didn't stop at redemption but added prayer. I'll call this minor or not report.
last_rejected.ruling: 'as well' reasonably conveys amplius; meaning preserved, mere weakening not major error.

last_rejected.quote: what would an innocent man ask for himself
last_rejected.source_quote: quid enim pro se innocens precaretur
last_rejected.why: Latin 'innocens' = 'innocent one'/'guiltless one.' English 'an innocent man' adds 'man' which is reasonable. 'precaretur' = 'would pray'/'would ask.' English 'ask' for 'precaretur'—but earlier 'Orabat... et rogabat' = 'was praying and asking.' The English uses 'ask' for both 'rogabat' and 'precaretur,' losing the distinction between 'precari' (pray) and 'rogare' (ask/beseech). But this is minor. Hmm. Let me check 'pro se' = 'for himself.' Correct. 'quid enim' = 'for what.' Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: 'ask' is within precari's normal range; 'man' is reasonable for innocens. No meaning lost.
